## Goal

Help a researcher distinguish relevant venues from superficially similar ones using official scope and article-type guidance.

**For:** a public-health, health-services, education or behavioral researcher. **First attempt:** 20–30 minutes.

## Start

Use the [directory](https://open-source-research-initiative.github.io/venues/) in its default mode, filter to your field and compare three venues for a clearly described public research example.

## Return

- The research example, field and intended article type, plus the comparison URL.
- Three official scope/article-type links, one per venue.
- A brief source-backed reason each venue fits or should be excluded. Include important author, research-focus or article-type restrictions.
- Which statements are the venue's rules and which are your own assessment.

## Acceptance

A comparison that identifies meaningful fit or restrictions and makes no acceptance-probability claim. It can become a public walkthrough only with permission for any participant-specific description or quotation. This scope check is distinct from the shorter interface trial: do not count the same work twice.

## How to take this task

Human maintainer: **Cole / @ajhcs**. Comment that you would like to help, and wait for a maintainer to confirm the claim before starting a substantial check. Claim one task at a time; the launch starts with at most three active claims across these issues. The timebox is a suggested first attempt. If a source is blocked or unclear, report that limit.

Reply here with a short note and source links. **No code, installation, fork or pull request is required.** Include the date checked and any material AI/agent assistance. Please use only information you may share publicly; a public research-topic description is enough. For an email route without a GitHub account, contact [Cole](mailto:cole.lyons@pennmedicine.upenn.edu?subject=OSRI%20venue%20directory%20task).

Cole reviews the evidence and acceptance. Maintainers prepare any data changes and dated follow-up records; a comment does not automatically change a venue's status. Useful confirmation of an existing record can count. Public credit is optional: say which handle/name you prefer, or request no public credit. Accepted work is recorded once per agreed task under [OSRI's contribution rules](https://github.com/Open-Source-Research-Initiative/osri/blob/main/community/README.md); it does not promise authorship.

Prepared with Codex assistance for the human-directed OSRI launch. This is an open task, not an accepted contribution.

## Goal

Document a traceable publication sample for **Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics**. Its current directory assessment has an unresolved publication-sample check.

**For:** someone comfortable locating an article and DOI. **First attempt:** 15–20 minutes.

## Start

Open the [official journal information](https://publishingsupport.iopscience.iop.org/journals/journal-of-physics-d-applied-physics/) and follow the journal homepage or contents links. If the publisher page cannot be read, an exact-journal Crossref metadata record is an alternative; identify that limitation.

## Return

- One recent research article's title, DOI and journal identity.
- Publication date if available, plus a publisher landing page or exact Crossref record.
- Whether the check used a publisher page or metadata only; report blocked pages accurately.

## Acceptance

A reproducible bibliographic match to this journal. DOI metadata establishes traceability within its limits; it does not establish scientific validity, the quality of the article, or how peer review actually occurred.

## Goal

Independently document current named editorial leadership for **International Relations**. The directory currently records this as an unresolved core check; missing accessible evidence is not a misconduct finding.

**For:** someone able to inspect a journal board page. **First attempt:** 20 minutes.

## Start

Use the [official editorial board](https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/ire). Check that it is International Relations, not a similarly named journal.

## Return

- At least one current named editor, the stated role, and affiliation where available.
- Exact official source URL, journal identity and date checked.
- Any access or identity problem; leave unstated affiliations missing.

## Acceptance

Readable evidence matching the correct journal, or a substantive access finding that helps maintainers reproduce the problem. Maintainers assess whether a dated follow-up resolves the recorded gap; the note alone does not promote the venue.

## Goal

Check what **Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS)** permits and what authors must disclose. Preserve the distinction between research, analysis/code, drafting and language editing.

**For:** a researcher or research-software contributor. **First attempt:** 20 minutes.

## Start

Read the [official JOSS submission guidance](https://joss.readthedocs.io/en/latest/submitting.html), including its AI policy and any directly linked instructions.

## Return

- The AI uses explicitly addressed and the restrictions attached to them.
- What authors must disclose, where the disclosure goes, and whether different instructions apply to software and the paper.
- Exact official section links and date checked.
- Any permission that remains unclear. Do not generalize language-editing permission into permission for substantive research or drafting.

## Acceptance

A concise policy note whose interpretation can be checked from the linked text. This task reviews instructions; it does not scientifically review a software paper or establish unrestricted AI permission.

## Goal

Check the author-cost record for **Research Ethics**, keeping submission and publication costs separate.

**For:** someone comfortable reading author instructions. **First attempt:** 15 minutes.

## Start

Read the [official submission guidelines](https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/rea), especially publishing fees. Confirm the journal identity before following publisher-wide links. You do not need to contact the journal or make a submission.

## Return

- Submission cost and standard publication cost as two separate findings.
- Applicable article types and any compulsory page, membership, registration or other charges.
- Whether an option is mandatory, optional open access, or conditional on funding/waiver eligibility. Reader subscription costs are a separate matter.
- Official URLs, relevant section names, date checked, and anything the evidence does not establish. A short paraphrase is enough; do not copy entire pages.

## Acceptance

A source-backed note another reader can reproduce. Confirmation of the current record is useful. Silence about a charge does not prove zero cost. Maintainers independently review the finding and add dated follow-up evidence without rewriting the historical cost campaign.

## Goal

Help us find out whether the directory helps a researcher choose plausible publication venues. We want honest outcomes, including “none fits.”

**For:** a researcher with a current or planned paper. **First attempt:** 10–15 minutes.

## Start

Open the [venue directory](https://open-source-research-initiative.github.io/venues/). Select your field, read the scope and conditions, and compare up to three venues. Use a public topic or a description you are comfortable sharing; do not upload a manuscript.

## Return

- Research field and article type, with a brief public topic description.
- A shortlist/comparison URL, or the filters used if nothing fits.
- One plausible venue and why it fits, or why none does. Note relevant cost, scope, author-eligibility or AI-disclosure conditions.
- One confusing step, missing fact or helpful detail; say where you needed an explanation.

## Acceptance

An actual use report with an actionable observation. A visit or “looks good” alone is insufficient; a well-explained no-fit result is useful. This issue can host more than one pilot report if maintainers agree distinct tasks with participants. We will ask separately before quoting your experience publicly.
